The sun is a star that gives us light and heat. Without it there would be no plants, no animals and no people on Earth. The planets travel around the sun in big circles that we call orbits.
Water can be a liquid, a solid or a gas. When it is very cold, it turns into ice. When it gets hot, it becomes steam. This change is part of the water cycle that gives life to our planet.

Our body is like a machine that never rests. The heart pumps blood, the lungs bring in air and the brain sends orders to every part. Sleeping well and eating healthy food helps this machine work better.
Scientists observe, ask questions and do experiments to understand the world. They write down what they see and share their discoveries, so that other people can learn from them and keep exploring.
Bees live in big families called colonies. Each bee has a job: some look for flowers, others take care of the babies and others build the hive. Thanks to their work we have honey and many fruits.
The whale is the biggest animal on the planet. Even though it lives in the sea, it is not a fish: it breathes air and feeds its babies with milk. Its song can travel very far under the water.
Dogs have been friends of people for thousands of years. They are loyal, playful and very smart. A dog can learn many tricks, help people who cannot see and even find lost children in the mountains.

Colombia is a country full of colors, music and nature. It has beaches, snowy mountains, deserts and a huge rainforest. Its people are known for being friendly, and its coffee is loved around the world.
The Andes mountains split into three ranges when they enter Colombia. Between them flow the Magdalena and Cauca rivers, which bring water to many towns and farms and help grow food all year long.

Every year, many cities in Colombia hold colorful festivals. There are parades, costumes, dances and music for everyone. These celebrations show the history and the traditions of each region of the country.
A forest is much more than a group of trees. It is a home for birds, insects and mammals. The trees clean the air, protect the soil from the rain and give us wood, fruit and shade on hot days.

Rivers begin as tiny drops in the high mountains. They join together, run down the hills and finally reach the sea. Along the way they give water to plants, animals and people, so we must keep them clean.

Typing without looking at the keys is a skill that you can learn with practice. At first you go slowly, but after a few weeks your fingers remember where each letter is, and you can write faster and with fewer mistakes.

A computer follows instructions that people write. These instructions are called programs. With a program we can draw, write, play music, talk to friends far away and learn about almost anything in the world.

Once upon a time there was a curious fox who lived at the edge of a forest. Every night she looked at the stars and wondered how far they were. One day she decided to climb the tallest hill to see them closer.

Lucy loved to read. She read at breakfast, on the bus and even under the covers with a flashlight. One afternoon she found an old book in the library. When she opened it, a tiny dragon jumped out and said hello.
The little robot woke up in the middle of a big, quiet junkyard. He did not remember his name or where his home was. So he picked up a wrench, turned on his lamp and began to look for his friends.

On the first day of school, Tom felt very nervous. He did not know anyone. Then a girl smiled at him and shared her colored pencils. By the end of the day they were friends, and the school did not seem so big.

Being a good teammate means helping others, even when we are not winning. A good team listens, shares the ball and celebrates every goal together. What matters most is to play fair and to enjoy the game with our friends.

Honesty is telling the truth even when it is hard. When we are honest, people trust us and we feel calm inside. Everyone makes mistakes, but the brave ones say sorry and try to do better the next time.

Long ago, people wrote on clay, on stone and later on paper. The printing press let books travel to many places, and more people could learn to read. Today we also write on screens, and our fingers do the work.

The first keyboards were made for typewriters more than one hundred years ago. The letters were placed in the order we still use today. That is why the QWERTY keyboard is found on computers all over the world.

Our solar system has eight planets. Mercury is the closest to the sun and Neptune is the farthest. Jupiter is so big that more than one thousand Earths could fit inside it. Astronauts dream of visiting them one day.

A healthy plate has many colors. Fruits and vegetables give us vitamins, rice and bread give us energy, and beans, eggs or fish help our muscles grow. Drinking water and eating together with family is also good for us.

Playing sports helps our body and our mind. We run, jump and breathe more deeply, and we also learn to follow rules, to work in a team and to accept a loss without getting angry. Moving every day makes us stronger and happier.

There are 7 days in a week and 12 months in a year. A year has 365 days, and every 4 years February gets one extra day. In one hour there are 60 minutes, and in one minute there are 60 seconds.
